questions.question: What is the defining feature of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It speeds up the reaction without being used up or chemically changed.
It slows down the reaction and is consumed by the end.
It permanently increases the temperature of the reaction mixture.
It changes the final products into different substances.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the specificity of catalysts?
options: Any catalyst can speed up any chemical reaction.
Different reactions require different, specific catalysts.
Catalysts only work for reactions that produce gases.
All catalysts are made of the exact same element.

questions.question: What are biological catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells called?
options: Monomers
Polymers
Enzymes
Alloys

questions.question: If metal X is more reactive than metal Y, what will happen when metal X is added to a solution of metal Y's salt?
options: No reaction will take place between the metals.
Metal X will displace metal Y from its salt.
Metal Y will displace metal X from its salt.
Both metals will dissolve to form a gas.

questions.question: In a displacement reaction, what are the products when magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution?
options: Magnesium oxide and copper sulfide
Copper sulfate and magnesium oxide
Magnesium sulfate solution and copper
Magnesium hydroxide and copper gas

questions.question: How can displacement reactions be used in the laboratory to study metals?
options: To confirm the position of a metal in the reactivity series
To determine the exact thermal conductivity of a metal
To turn non-metals into reactive metals
To measure the density of a metal ore

questions.question: What is a metal ore typically defined as?
options: A pure metal found in its elemental state at the surface
A mixture of metals melted together to form a shiny solid
A rock that contains a metal in a form that can be extracted
A synthetic polymer that conducts electricity

questions.question: When can carbon be used to extract a metal from its ore?
options: Only when carbon is more reactive than the metal
Only when carbon is less reactive than the metal
Only when the metal ore is completely liquid
Carbon can always be used to extract any metal

questions.question: Which of the following describes the typical properties of metals?
options: Soft, dull, brittle, and poor thermal conductors
Strong, shiny, malleable, ductile, and good conductors
Liquid at room temperature, highly flexible, and non-conductive
Hard and brittle substances made from heating soft clays

questions.question: What are ceramics typically made from, and how do their properties change?
options: Made from soft substances, becoming hard and brittle when heated
Made from long polymer chains, becoming highly flexible when cooled
Made from mixtures of metals, becoming malleable when heated
Made from gases, becoming liquid when pressurized

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A pure metal element that has been highly polished
A mixture of elements including at least one metal
A natural polymer made from long chains of monomers
A ceramic material that has been heated to high temperatures

questions.question: What is the main reason for creating composite materials?
options: To combine materials to create a new material with improved properties
To break down complex compounds into their single elements
To make a material that is purely metallic and highly reactive
To convert a synthetic polymer into a natural ceramic

questions.question: How are polymers formed from monomers?
options: Small monomer molecules join together to form very long chains of atoms
Large ceramic pieces are crushed into small monomer particles
Metals are mixed with carbon to form a flexible alloy
Monomers are heated until they decompose into hydrogen gas

questions.question: What is the effect of adding a plasticiser to a polymer?
options: It forms strong cross-links that lock the molecules in place
It gets between polymer molecules, letting them move over each other more easily
It breaks the long chains down into separate individual monomers
It turns the polymer into a hard, brittle ceramic material

questions.question: What effect do cross-links between polymer molecules have on the polymer's properties?
options: They make the polymer softer and much more flexible
They make the polymer harder and less flexible
They cause the polymer to dissolve instantly in water
They reduce the melting point to below room temperature

questions.question: What is produced when some metals react with acid?
options: A metal hydroxide and oxygen gas
A metal salt and hydrogen gas
A metal oxide and water
A ceramic and a polymer
